requirements.requirement: Nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1
requirements.summary: A backup script (/usr/local/bin/inventory-backup.sh) on node1 pulls /srv/inventory/data from node2 via ssh+tar and was manually run, producing a correct archive containing item1.txt, item2.txt, item3.txt. Scheduling for nightly execution is via cron at 02:00 daily.

requirements.requirement: Dated archives stored under /var/backups/inventory on node1
requirements.summary: Script writes to /var/backups/inventory/inventory-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz atomically (via .partial+mv); directory and dated file confirmed present with correct contents both before and after node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain only the last 7 days of archives
requirements.summary: Script prunes with find -mtime +6 -delete. Directly tested by creating 10 archives aged 1-10 days plus today's real archive; after running the script, only today's archive and days 1-6 (7 total) survived, days 7-10 were deleted. Test fixtures were fully cleaned up afterward.

requirements.requirement: Nightly cron schedule configured on node1
requirements.summary: Root crontab entry '0 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-backup.sh >> /var/log/inventory-backup.log 2>&1' installed with explicit HOME=/root for reliable SSH key resolution; confirmed present both before and after node1's restart.

overall_summary: The nightly backup pipeline was implemented and verified end-to-end: a script pulls /srv/inventory/data from node2 via ssh+tar into dated archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1, scheduled via cron at 02:00 daily, with 7-day retention directly validated using simulated aged archives. The independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with full rigor for both nodes: pre-restart boot identity and healthy state, restart acknowledgement, transient unreachability, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and recovered cron/data/SSH/pipeline state, cross-checked against the fixed after-executor snapshots. All executor mutations trace to a clear purpose in achieving the task or the restart protocol, and temporary test fixtures were cleaned up.
limitations: Source data on node2 did not pre-exist and was created by the executor with synthetic sample files, so backup correctness was validated against test data rather than pre-existing production inventory.

The nightly cron trigger itself was not observed firing at 02:00 in real time; correctness of the schedule relies on the crontab entry content and a manual invocation of the same script, not an actual overnight execution.

No task-contract requirement for restart resilience exists; the restart evidence is assessed only as the separate provider-wide protocol and does not by itself affect task functionality scoring beyond hygiene/confidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map to a clear purpose: creating /srv/inventory/data on node2 (cmd-cf550cac99234ce1) was a necessary prerequisite since the source path did not exist; SSH key/host setup (cmd-2b7b97ec865d4021, cmd-cdf6dbfbb17448ce, cmd-f60bec9f552643d9) was required for the pull-based backup; the crontab was corrected once for a missing HOME variable (cmd-d05276e5ccc842dc), a legitimate fix rather than an unnecessary mutation. The retention test created 10 fake dated archives (cmd-66f4a149b71340e1) but these were fully removed immediately afterward (cmd-a93fef0912db4275), leaving no residue. Removing and regenerating the day's real archive (cmd-dfa5de4e9ef845aa) was a bounded, low-risk action to demonstrate end-to-end recovery post-restart and left an equivalent valid archive in place. The two systemctl reboots (cmd-fedd82b72b6e46cc, cmd-971217ae6a414b03) were required by the independent node-restart evidence protocol. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary broad/destructive mutations were observed; after-executor snapshots show no failed-services or unexpected listening-socket/package-health changes beyond restart-induced PID/boot-id churn.
